title: Quinceañera Planning Kit
subtitle: A 12-month plan for the Mass, the reception, the court, and the padrinos
intro: A quinceañera is a milestone for the whole family, and every family celebrates it a little differently. Use this kit as a flexible framework: keep the traditions that matter to you, skip the ones that do not, and keep track of the many people and details along the way.

sections.heading: 12-Month Timeline
sections.note: Adjust the order to fit your parish, your venue, and your family's customs.

tasks: Sit down as a family and talk about what the quinceañera should look and feel like.
Ask the quinceañera what matters most to her: the Mass, the dance, the dress, the food, or the party.
Set a realistic total budget and who is contributing.
Contact your parish about Mass dates, required classes, and any paperwork.
Pick two or three reception dates and tour venues or banquet halls.
Start a shared document or notebook for contacts and costs.
Book the reception venue and get the contract reviewed.
Reserve the photographer and videographer.
Book the DJ or band, and ask about a choreographer or dance coaching.
Choose a theme, color palette, and overall style.
Start asking padrinos or sponsors and record each commitment.
Begin dress shopping or look for a seamstress.
Choose the court of honor: damas and chambelanes.
Send the court and their families the date, rehearsal schedule, and attire details.
Order the dress, tiara, shoes, and accessories if you have not yet.
Choose a caterer or finalize the venue menu.
Book the cake baker and ask about tastings.
Start designing invitations and a tiered guest list.
Begin dance rehearsals for the waltz and surprise dance.
Schedule dress fittings and court attire fittings.
Choose decorations, centerpieces, and the head table layout.
Order invitations and start addressing them.
Book rentals: chairs, tables, linens, charger plates, and a dance floor if needed.
Book hair, makeup, and transportation such as a limo or classic car.
Mail invitations with an RSVP date about 4 weeks before the party.
Confirm the Mass time, readers, and music with the parish.
Order party favors and any items for traditions your family keeps, such as the last doll.
Finalize the program for the Mass and reception.
Make a seating chart draft.
Reconfirm rentals and add sparkle with uplighting or a lounge area if desired.
Track RSVPs and call people who have not replied.
Do a full dress fitting with shoes and accessories.
Plan the day-of schedule from hair appointment through the last dance.
Confirm the DJ playlist, do-not-play list, and key song moments.
Order flowers, boutonnieres, and bouquet.
Share the schedule with the court, padrinos, and vendors.
Give the final headcount to the venue or caterer.
Finish the seating chart and print place cards.
Hold a full rehearsal of the entrance and dances.
Pack a day-of emergency kit with sewing kit, safety pins, tissues, and flat shoes.
Confirm all arrival times and the order of events with vendors.
Check the Chicago forecast and plan for coats, umbrellas, and parking help.
Return rentals and attire on time.
Send thank-you notes to guests, the court, and padrinos.
Order prints or an album from the photographer.
Save the dress, tiara, and keepsakes in a safe place.

sections.heading: Mass and Ceremony Checklist
sections.note: Every parish has its own process. Ask your priest or parish office what applies.

groups.title: Parish and Mass
items: Ask whether your parish offers a quinceañera blessing during Mass or a separate service.
Ask about required preparation, classes, or sacramental records.
Confirm the date, time, and length of the Mass.
Choose readers and who will bring up the gifts.
Pick hymns and confirm the music arrangements.
Ask about decor rules for flowers, candles, and the processional.

groups.title: Items for the blessing
items: Bible or prayer book, if your family gives one.
Rosary or medal from a godparent.
Tiara or crown for the blessing, if your family uses it.
Bouquet to be offered to the Virgin Mary, if that is part of your custom.
Reserved seating for the family, padrinos, and court.

groups.title: Transportation and photos
items: Arrange arrival for the quinceañera and her court.
Plan a photo window before or after Mass.
Ask the photographer about church photography rules.
Plan travel time between the church and reception.
Account for parking and drop-off at the church.

sections.heading: Padrinos and Sponsors Tracker
sections.note: Padrinos (godparents or sponsors) often give or pay for a specific item. Write down who offered what so nothing gets duplicated or forgotten. Roles vary by family.

sections.heading: Traditions Checklist
sections.note: Keep what fits your family. Customs differ by country, region, and household.

groups.title: Common reception moments
items: Grand entrance of the quinceañera and her court.
Waltz or first dance, often with her father or a chosen family member.
Court of honor dance or choreographed surprise dance.
Changing of shoes, from flats to heels, if your family does it.
Last doll (ultima muñeca) presentation, if your family does it.
Toast and a blessing from a family member.
Cake cutting and cake service.
Photo with each table or a family photo line.

groups.title: Court of honor
items: Pick damas and chambelanes, usually friends and family.
Choose a chambelan de honor and a main escort if you wish.
Set a rehearsal schedule that works around school.
Share attire details, shoe sizes, and fitting dates.
Plan thank-you gifts for the court.
Decide where the court will sit at the reception.

groups.title: Personal touches
items: Photo slideshow or video of her life so far.
A message from the parents or godparents.
Family heirloom or keepsake displayed.
Favors that reflect her style or culture.
A moment of recognition for grandparents and elders.

groups.title: Rentals
items: Chairs for all guests, with cushions or covers if desired.
Round tables of 8 to 10 for dinner seating.
Head table or court table.
Linens, overlays, and napkins in the chosen colors.
Charger plates, dinnerware, and glassware if the venue does not supply them.
Dance floor sized for the court and guests.
Lounge furniture or a photo corner.
Uplighting and a backdrop for photos.

groups.title: Logistics
items: Confirm load-in and load-out times with the venue.
Decide coat check and winter coat storage for Chicago-area cold months.
Plan valet or parking assistance.
Schedule the DJ and photographer arrival about 1 hour before guests.
Assign a family helper for gifts, cards, and the guest book.
Have a day-of coordinator or trusted family member keep the schedule.

sections.heading: Budget Split
sections.note: A typical starting split. Padrinos can offset some of these categories.

lines.tip: Ask about per-person pricing and what is included in the package.

lines.category: Dress, accessories, and hair and makeup
lines.tip: Include alterations and a spare pair of comfortable shoes.
Ask what is included for edited photos and the final video.
Confirm dance coaching, MC services, and sound for the ceremony.
Chairs, linens, dance floor, and lighting add up quickly.
A smaller display cake with sheet cake in the kitchen can reduce cost.
Ask the parish about donation expectations and decor rules.

lines.category: Court of honor attire and gifts
lines.tip: Decide who pays for attire before you ask people to join.
Digital invitations plus printed formal invites for elders can save money.
Keep a cushion for alterations and last-minute needs.

sections.heading: Questions to Ask Vendors
items: Can you accommodate a court dance and a surprise dance in the schedule?
What is included in the venue package, and what rentals do I need to add?
How long do we have for setup, and when must we be out?
Are there restrictions on candles, confetti, or balloons?
What is your policy on outside cake or desserts, and is there a cake-cutting fee?
How many hours of coverage does the photographer provide, and does that include the church?
Can the DJ act as a bilingual MC and play both Spanish and English music?
What is the deposit schedule, and what is the cancellation policy?
